questions.question_text: How long does the IELTS Speaking test typically last?
questions.explanation: The IELTS Speaking test is a face-to-face session that lasts between 11 and 14 minutes.

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT one of the criteria used to assess the Speaking section?
questions.explanation: Speaking is assessed on Fluency/coherence, Lexical resource, Grammatical range/accuracy, and Pronunciation. Writing speed is not a criterion.

questions.question_text: Can a test taker use sign language during the Speaking test?
options: No, sign language is not permitted.
Only if they have a speech impairment.
Yes, if they are also taking the Writing test.
questions.explanation: The IELTS guidelines clearly state that signing is not allowed during the Speaking test.

questions.question_text: How long does the IELTS Speaking test usually last?
questions.explanation: The Speaking section is a face-to-face interview that typically ranges between 11 and 14 minutes.

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT an assessment criterion for the Speaking section?
questions.explanation: Examiners assess Speaking based on Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Pronunciation.

questions.question_text: Is the use of sign language permitted in the Speaking test?
options: Yes, if an interpreter is provided
questions.explanation: The regulations for IELTS clearly state that sign language cannot be used as a method of communication during the Speaking test.

questions.question_text: How are the four criteria for the Speaking test weighted?
questions.explanation: Each of the four Speaking assessment criteria is weighted equally to calculate the final score.

questions.question_text: What can a candidate with a hearing or speech impairment request for the Speaking test?
options: Extra time to read materials or decide on a response
To skip the test entirely without penalty
Use of a written script during the interview
questions.explanation: Candidates with specific impairments may request extra time to process the material or prepare their responses during the Speaking test.

questions.question_text: What is the format of the Speaking section?
options: A face-to-face session with a trained examiner
questions.explanation: The IELTS Speaking test is conducted as a face-to-face interview with a qualified IELTS examiner.

questions.question_text: What happens if a candidate feels nervous during the Speaking test?
options: They must stop the test immediately
The examiner helps them feel comfortable so they can perform their best
They are given a lower score
questions.explanation: Examiners are trained to help candidates feel comfortable and relaxed to ensure the test accurately reflects their ability.

questions.question_text: Are IELTS tests assessed by computers or humans?
options: A mix of computer and human algorithms
questions.explanation: IELTS prides itself on assessment by trained, real-world examiners rather than computer-based evaluation for Speaking.

questions.question_text: Does the Speaking test format differ between Academic and General Training?
options: No, it is the same for both test types
questions.explanation: The Speaking and Listening components are identical in structure and content for both the Academic and General Training tests.

questions.question_text: How is the final score for the Speaking section determined?
options: It is the average of the four assessment criteria
It is determined solely by grammar
It is based on the speed of speech
It is decided by an automated system
questions.explanation: The final Speaking score is the result of averaging the marks given for each of the four assessment criteria.

questions.question_text: Can a candidate ask for the Speaking task card in Braille?
options: Yes, if they have a visual impairment
Only if they have a speech impairment
questions.explanation: Candidates with visual impairments are permitted to request Speaking test task cards in Braille or enlarged print.

questions.question_text: Are speaking tests conducted via video call in any format?
options: Yes, for paper-based tests in all locations
Only if the candidate is sick
questions.explanation: For the IELTS Online test, the Speaking section is conducted through a video call with a trained examiner.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a focus area for the Speaking test assessment?
questions.explanation: Lexical resource is one of the four key criteria used to award a band score in the Speaking test.

questions.question_text: What is the primary goal of the Speaking test?
options: To test the ability to recite poems
To assess the ability to have real conversations in English
To test the ability to interpret written graphs
To check the ability to sing
questions.explanation: The Speaking test is designed to evaluate how well a test taker can engage in genuine conversational English.

questions.question_text: Does an examiner provide feedback during the Speaking test?
options: Yes, they explain mistakes as they happen
No, the examiner assesses but does not provide immediate feedback
Yes, they provide a summary at the end
questions.explanation: The examiner is there to conduct the test and evaluate the candidate; they do not provide feedback during the session.

questions.question_text: How are the four assessment criteria for the Speaking test weighted?
options: Each of the criteria carry equal weighting
questions.explanation: Each of the four criteria in the Speaking test carries equal weighting in the final score.
